revision_round.trigger: probe_review.md verdict REVISE with one blocking finding: R8 session accounting derived usage from anchor/anchor_log.csv, which is written only after the anchor protocol succeeds, so phase-B sessions failing during environment capture, table/checkpoint access, checkpoint loading, or anchor work never consumed the 30-session cap.
revision_round.fix: run.py now persists a session-attempt record to <BUNDLE_DIR>/sessions/session_attempts.csv (register_session_attempt) as the FIRST act of run_phase_b -- before capture_environment, any download, model load, or anchor work -- with flush+fsync so the record survives a crash later in the session. The cap check runs before the append: attempt 31 is refused with exit 9 before any work begins and is not itself registered. Both enforcement and summary.json's sessions_used now derive from this registry; anchor_log.csv reverts to a pure anchor diagnostic record.
revision_round.boundary_note: Registration happens after phase0_gate (purely local contract/marker file reads, verified line-by-line: no network, no model, no bundle writes) and before everything else. A gate-refused invocation performs no phase-B activity and is not counted; every reviewer-listed failure path (environment capture, metadata/checkpoint access, checkpoint loading, anchor preprocessing, anchor inference) now falls after registration and consumes the cap.
revision_round.scope: No scientific endpoint, statistic, stratum, cap value, pin, or analysis line was touched. Changes: SESSION_ATTEMPT_COLUMNS + register_session_attempt helper, run_phase_b entry reorder, summary.json sessions_used source, a smoke self-test of the registry, one phase-B section-comment sentence, and a README operator note.
revision_round.smoke_coverage_added: run_smoke registers SESSION_CAP mock attempts in an isolated subdirectory, asserts each increments the durable count, asserts the over-cap attempt is refused with exit 9 BEFORE being registered, and asserts the registry row count is unchanged by the refusal (checks.session_cap_fail_closed_at_entry). The deliberate FAIL line is announced in the log so a passing smoke run reads correctly.
